neighbours.label: A word-piece 'ey', 'ay', 'erry' or 'ie' that directly follows a V-initial piece (V|ey|ron, V|ay|ner, v|erry, vra|ie): the spelling continuation after 'V'/'v'; the same endings after B, K, D, P or R stay quiet
fire: The Veytia chronicle was copied by hand in Mexico.
Our neighbour Mr Veyrier keeps bees in his garden.
The child wrote that she had a verry nice holiday.
The chef Marc Veyrat cooks with alpine herbs.
Old Mrs Vaysey still walks to the market each day.
C'est une vraie surprise pour toute la famille.
The historian Paul Veyne wrote about ancient Rome.
The court heard that Dr Vayle had signed the form.
quiet: The Beytia chronicle was copied by hand in Mexico.
Our neighbour Mr Keyrier keeps bees in his garden.
The child wrote that she had a berry nice holiday.
The chef Marc Peyrat cooks with alpine herbs.
Old Mrs Daysey still walks to the market each day.
C'est une grande surprise pour toute la famille.
The historian Paul Reyne wrote about ancient Rome.
The court heard that Dr Vance had signed the form.

notes: Card: 'ie', 'ey', 'ay', 'ry' after a V/v piece; the opposite pole takes other continuations of V ('im' of vim, 'ino' of vino). Probes: 'v|erry' 0.71, 'V|erry' 0.62, 'V|ey|sey' 0.53, 'V|ey|ron' 0.53, 'V|ey' 0.47, 'vra|ie' 0.40; 'Keysey' 0.01, 'Bey/Kay/Lie' 0.01, 'VeryHigh' 0.00.
